verification.initial_result: Parent coordinator reports all runtime tests and eleven bins passed; initial formatting/lock gate failed. Exact remote formatting patch and Cargo.lock subsequently applied.
verification.remaining: Final clean CI must include the fallible SQLite foreign-key iterator correction and all final article sources. No publication approval or reviewed hashes.
verification.snippet_sync: All eleven article fences copied from source markers after remote formatting; no local formatter executed.

self_review: Each draft starts from its own concrete failure or storage need; 904–1026-word initial range was checked without padding.
Removed abstract first-pass phrasing and canned closing lines; did not invent author experiences or language mistakes.
All fenced executable snippets are Rust; SQL is inside Rust strings.
Prose distinguishes actual database checks from workload performance, durable delivery, operating-system isolation, and complete product implementations.

articles.verification_notes: Checks committed balances and transfer count after success, oversized/negative requests, duplicate-key rollback, and a direct CHECK violation.
limitations: Fixed demonstration accounts and integer credits; not a payment system or full idempotent endpoint.
Pool cap is per pool, not a fleet-wide capacity limit.
Does not cover authorization, crash recovery, or opposite-order transfer deadlocks.

articles.verification_notes: Creates a versioned local schema; verifies a committed note after close/reopen, an absent rolled-back note, and rejection of an invalid done flag.
limitations: Connection close/reopen is not an OS restart or power-loss test.
First insert ID one follows the new empty fixture; production code should obtain the inserted ID.
No backup implementation, encryption, file-permission enforcement, or cross-machine sharing.

articles.verification_notes: Two acquired connections explicitly place committed writes between reader statements, checking Read Committed and Repeatable Read results before and after commit.
limitations: Ordinary primary-database reads only; not caches, replicas, or every locking clause.
Stable snapshots are not a complete read-then-write business invariant.
Uses PostgreSQL 18 semantics and a tiny controlled table; no performance claim.

articles.verification_notes: A different connection commits between the serializable attempt's read and write; expected two attempts, reads [0,1], and final counter 2.
limitations: The first-attempt intervention is test harness coordination, not production retry behavior.
Retries only received SQLSTATE 40001; not an unknown commit result or arbitrary network error.
No external effects, complete outbox, adaptive backoff, or contention benchmark.

articles.verification_notes: Reads pg_stat_xact_user_tables inside one writing transaction, expecting (updates,HOT) (10,10) then (11,10), and verifies final row contents.
limitations: Current-transaction view avoids cumulative-stat flush/snapshot lag; does not claim cumulative counters update synchronously.
One small row, ample page room, B-tree indexes, fillfactor50; not a production HOT ratio.
No timing, WAL-byte, vacuum, table-size, or overall index-benefit measurements.

articles.verification_notes: Uses a separate application login, verifies non-owner/non-superuser/non-BYPASSRLS, allowed reads for both tenants, missing context denial, pooled context reset, and forbidden insert.
limitations: Trusted application selects tenant context; hostile SQL under that role can set the custom context.
Owner bypass is deliberately visible; FORCE does not constrain superusers/BYPASSRLS.
One app connection makes reuse visible; not complete authorization for functions/views/admin paths.

articles.verification_notes: Live listener receives work1 event; fresh listener after work2 commit finds no historical event but recovers work2 from table; next live event and pending scan work.
limitations: Dropping/recreating a listener object is a controlled absence, not every physical network-failure mode.
One consumer, no atomic multiworker claim or crash-safe external effect.
100ms absence window is a bounded fixture wait, not a production latency measurement.

articles.verification_notes: Checks SQLSTATE55P04 before added enum label commits, successful committed storage, and unchanged old manual decoder accepting pending but rejecting processing.
limitations: Manual text-to-Rust decoder, not SQLx derive implementation or real released binary.
Does not implement fleet rollout gates or a compatibility presenter.
No simplistic down-migration promise; committed new-state data remains after disabling a writer.

articles.verification_notes: Two connections and explicit writer ownership check old committed reads, DatabaseBusy, BUSY_SNAPSHOT, rollback, and fresh-write success.
limitations: Local temporary WAL file; no network filesystem or load benchmark.
Finite busy timeout is a failure bound, not a precise elapsed-time assertion or universal tuning value.
Does not implement a general retry framework or transaction-coupled external effects.

articles.verification_notes: On current-thread Tokio, one worker owns rusqlite; submitted write cannot finish while external writer holds lock; heartbeat progresses, two queued slots fill, excess job rejects, later replies show one note.
limitations: Readiness signal precedes SQLite execute; proves async progress while database request is pending, not a trace of the exact driver wait-start instant.
One thread/two-slot queue with fixed small jobs; not a payload-byte budget or throughput result.
Dropping reply/caller timeout does not cancel started SQLite work; no complete shutdown/cancellation framework.

articles.verification_notes: Deliberately disabled connection stores orphan; checked open finds existing violation and rejects new ones; RESTRICT/CASCADE and reopened connection enforced; enable-in-transaction remains ineffective.
limitations: Does not repair old orphans automatically or authorize a user's project.
No arbitrary external writer initialization guarantee or large-cascade performance test.
After initial CI, fallible foreign_key_check iteration was changed to collect Result<Vec<_>> before counting; final CI must include that correction.
